A 65-year-old male patient is seen for follow-up one week after hospital discharge for a properly treated
ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). He has not taken any prescribed medications or attended
his scheduled follow-up appointment. His medical history includes hypertension and peripheral
vascular disease. His vital signs show: temperature 98.9°F (36.4°C), blood pressure 183/105 mmHg,
heart rate 90/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Physical
examination reveals jugular venous distention and bilateral lower extremity pitting edema. His
echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 55%. Which medication would provide the greatest
reduction in mortality for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Carvedilol (B) Amlodipine (C) Diltiazem (D)
Losartan (E) Lisinopril (F) Digoxin (G) Spironolactone (H) Propranolol (I) Hydralazine and isosorbide
dinitrate (J) Metoprolol succinate
 A. Losartan
B. Hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate
C. Lisinopril
D. Metoprolol succinate
E. Amlodipine
F. Carvedilol
G. Diltiazem
H. Digoxin
I. Spironolactone
J. Propranolol
